statement.p: The boundaries of the shaded region are the y-axis, the line y = 1, and the curve y=\sqrt[4]{x}.

description.p: The region in the x-y-plane. The shaded region looks like a triangle with a curved side and seems to have vertices at the origin, (0,1) and (1,1). The top boundary of the region is the horizontal line y=1, the left boundary of the region is the y-axis, and the bottom boundary of the region is the function y=\sqrt[4]{x}.

statement.p: This area can be computed in two different ways using integrals.
First, it can be computed as an integral with respect to x, \int_a^b [f(x)- g(x)]\,dx
Alternatively, this area can be computed as an integral with respect to y, \int_{c}^{d} h(y)\,dy where c = , d = and
Either way we find that the area is .

solution.p: Looking at the region, x starts at a=0 and ends at b=1, and the higher y-value is the line y=1, while the lower y-value is y=\sqrt[4]{x}. So the integral is \displaystyle \int_0^1 \left[1-\sqrt[4]{x}\right] \ dx

Looking at the region again, y starts at c=0 and ends at d=1, and x goes from 0 on the left side of the region to the graph of y=\sqrt[4]{x} on the right. But that has x in it, so we solve for x and get x=y^4. So the integral is \displaystyle \int_0^1 y^4 \ dy
We could solve either integral, but I'll pick the one in terms of y. \displaystyle \int_0^1 y^4 \ dy = \frac{y^5}{5} \biggr|_0^1 = \frac{1}{5}
